title: One Listen line, a fleet of dead Apaches
role: You are on the SRE team of a large wiki site. Puppet manages Apache on hundreds of application servers and on a few other web hosts.
brief: 11:40 UTC. A colleague merges a Puppet change to the Apache configuration. At 11:45 a probe alert fires for a port-443 service, and IRC starts filling with alerts.

steps.situation: Hosts that just ran Puppet show `apache2.service` failed and connection refused on port 80. The others haven't run Puppet yet.
steps.evidence:
$ systemctl is-failed apache2
failed
$ curl -sI http://localhost/ | head -1
curl: (7) Failed to connect to localhost port 80: Connection refused
$ grep -n '^Listen' /etc/apache2/ports.conf
5:Listen 80
6:Listen 443

choices.text: Stop it spreading: disable the Puppet agent on the app servers before the next runs
choices.why: This is what was done at 11:45. Every host that runs Puppet next would break the same way; stopping the agent buys you time.
Apache reads the same bad config and fails again, and healthy hosts get a restart they didn't need.

choices.text: Wait for the next Puppet run to settle it
choices.why: The next run is what breaks the remaining hosts.

steps.situation: The revert merged at 11:46 and you forced a Puppet run. The broken hosts are still down.

choices.text: Look at one broken host: what is in ports.conf now, does apachectl configtest pass, is the service even running?
choices.why: A revert changes what future runs write. On these hosts the bad `Listen 443` line stayed and Apache stayed stopped, so the revert alone fixed nothing.

choices.text: The revert must be wrong: revert the revert and try again
choices.why: You are back to the broken change, without having looked at a single host.
Apache starts at boot with the same ports.conf and fails the same way.

steps.situation: Cause found by 11:50: the change makes Apache listen on 443 even where mod_ssl is not enabled. A subset of the app servers is down.

choices.text: One scripted command over the fleet tool: remove the line, start Apache. Then a proper patch for the other servers
choices.why: Run at 11:56; first recoveries came a minute later. A proper fix for hosts on Debian's default config followed at 12:05 and was tested on one host first.

choices.text: SSH to each host and edit the file by hand
choices.why: It works, slowly, and by host 30 someone makes a typo.

choices.text: Enable Puppet again and let it fix things
choices.why: You already saw that a run doesn't remove the line or start the service.

steps.situation: All healthy at 12:16. The catalog compiled fine in the pre-merge check, so the check passed. What do you change?

choices.text: A canary group that gets Puppet changes first, and careful review for patches that touch service config
choices.why: The report's gaps: the patch wasn't reviewed carefully, and there's no controlled place to try Puppet changes. A compiling catalog can still produce a config Apache rejects.

choices.text: Add apachectl configtest to the Puppet run before any restart
choices.why: Worth adding, but it checks syntax, and an extra `Listen 443` is valid syntax: Apache failed when it started. Apache's docs warn that a clean configtest doesn't promise a clean restart. Keep the canary.

choices.text: Freeze all Apache changes for a month
choices.why: Changes pile up and the next one is bigger. Make changes safer, not rarer.

debrief.what_happened: On 24 May 2022 at 11:40 UTC a Puppet change was merged that made Apache listen on port 443 whether or not mod_ssl was enabled. Apache failed to restart on the hosts that applied it. About 140 alerts reached IRC (connection refused on port 80), and a very small number of 502s hit mostly logged-in users. At 11:45 the author realised what had happened and Puppet was disabled on the MediaWiki hosts; the revert merged at 11:46 did not repair hosts already broken. At 11:56 a Cumin command removed `Listen 443` from `/etc/apache2/ports.conf` and started Apache; the app servers were fixed by 11:58. A proper fix for non-MediaWiki servers that use Debian's default config was merged at 12:05, tested on one host at 12:07, and all were healthy at 12:16. The catalog compiler passed because the catalog compiled; the problem was the resulting Apache config. The report names the gaps: careless review and no canary environment for Puppet changes.
lessons: When config management spreads a bad change, stop the agent before you fix hosts.
A revert fixes future runs; check what is on the broken hosts now.
"It compiles" is not "Apache starts": test the rendered config.
Roll config changes to a canary group first.
